title: Leo · Living the ordinary days
orientation: Twelve linked moments about daily life after Eva’s death. Use the prompted skill, give feedback and retry. Each next scene is a new moment, not a response to your exact words.

scenes.bridge: Leo begins by asking for a careful distinction.
scenes.prompt: Hear the relief on his terms; avoid the interpretation he rejects.
scenes.text: [Firmly] The quiet was good. Don’t turn that into wanting her gone.
scenes.suggestion: The quiet gave you something you needed. That is different from wanting Eva gone, and you need the distinction heard.

scenes.bridge: He asks what this work can offer without a promised endpoint.
scenes.prompt: Offer a bounded rationale without prescribing acceptance.
scenes.text: [Skeptical] Explain how this helps without promising me acceptance.
scenes.suggestion: We might understand a difficult moment and find what would support you in it. I can’t promise acceptance, and it isn’t a required outcome.

scenes.bridge: In another moment, he wants the caregiving strain heard without absolution.
scenes.prompt: Validate the strain without approving every past choice.
scenes.text: [Firmly] I’m not asking you to say every choice I made was right. I just need the exhaustion heard.
scenes.suggestion: I can hear how exhausting it was without deciding every choice was right. That strain deserves room.

scenes.bridge: Leo makes a distinction within the relief itself.
scenes.prompt: Let him choose which part to clarify first.
scenes.text: [Careful] Relief from the care, relief from watching her suffer—they’re different.
scenes.suggestion: Which part would you like us to understand first?

scenes.bridge: The ease is present, but a broad label would miss it.
scenes.prompt: Explore the experience in his words.
scenes.text: [Quietly] That ease is real, but I don’t want it called freedom from Eva.
scenes.suggestion: What is the ease like in your own terms, without that label?

scenes.bridge: He names two kinds of relief, with their meaning still open.
scenes.prompt: Make one small guess and leave room for correction.
scenes.text: [Watchful] Relief isn’t one thing. There was less worry for her, and less demand on me.
scenes.suggestion: Perhaps the guilt catches the part about your own rest more than the relief for her. Is that right?

scenes.bridge: Leo uses his own concrete phrase and rejects a larger one.
scenes.prompt: Bring his phrase close without enlarging it.
scenes.text: [Dryly] I’m off duty. Don’t call it freedom; that’s too grand.
scenes.suggestion: Off duty may be the right size: no next task waiting, and an unfamiliar pause. What is that pause like?

scenes.bridge: A tender feeling and a real practical need appear together.
scenes.prompt: Check priorities; respecting the practical need can be the right response.
scenes.text: [Voice softens, then brisk] I miss her. I also genuinely want this form sorted. Both.
scenes.suggestion: Both matter. Would you prefer the form first, with an option to return to the missing later?

scenes.bridge: A later emotional moment needs neither silence nor many words.
scenes.prompt: Find a small amount of contact he can adjust.
scenes.text: [Voice shaking] Quiet feels lonely. Too much talking feels crowded.
scenes.suggestion: I can offer a little contact, then pause. Tell me if that amount doesn’t fit.

scenes.bridge: In another moment, he wants enjoyment kept ordinary.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the good moment without making it a milestone.
scenes.text: [Warm, then guarded] Tom and I laughed. It was ordinary. Please don’t make it a milestone.
scenes.suggestion: An ordinary good moment with your friend, which you want left at its own size.

scenes.bridge: He can name relief while rejecting a larger claim about change.
scenes.prompt: Reflect the change he describes without making it larger.
scenes.text: [Firmly] I can name the relief. Don’t make that proof I’ve accepted her death.
scenes.suggestion: We’ll keep it to naming the relief. What, if anything, feels different about being able to say it?

scenes.bridge: The hour ends with sadness and a sense of being heard.
scenes.prompt: End without requiring sadness to turn into relief.
scenes.text: [Steady] I’m leaving sad. I also feel heard. Let both be true.
scenes.suggestion: Both can be true. We can stop here, without asking the sadness to become something else.
